question: In the Constitution of India, principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity were borrowed from:
solution:
The correct answer is __**the French Constitution.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Constitution of India, the principles of **Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity** were borrowed from the **French Constitution**. Here are the key points regarding these principles:

 
 
• **Liberty**: Refers to the freedom of Indian citizens to act as they choose, without oppressive restrictions.
 
• **Equality**: Emphasizes that no group in society should have special privileges and that all individuals should have equal opportunities.
 
• **Fraternity**: Represents a sense of brotherhood and a shared belonging among the citizens of the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** from **Ireland**.
 
• **Nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha** from **Ireland**.
 
• **Method of election of a president** from **Ireland**.
